{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZkoYkg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDLNfA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 73, "title": "Model Z80 WZ/MEMPTR state and correct BIT (HL) flags", "body": "## Problem

`crates/msx-core/src/cpu.rs` has no WZ/MEMPTR state. At lines 675–683, `BIT n,(HL)` derives undocumented F3/F5 from the memory operand; the selected Z80 behavior derives them from WZ bits 11/13. Substituting the current HL address would also be incorrect because earlier instructions determine WZ.

This affects shared CPU behavior across MSX1/MSX2 firmware, cartridge and disk execution. Compatibility impact is inferred; no specific commercial-game failure is established.

## Expected outcome

Maintain coherent instruction-dependent WZ state and use its high-byte bits 3/5 for `BIT n,(HL)`. Preserve operand-derived register BIT flags and effective-address-derived indexed BIT flags. Use a documented Zilog NMOS-compatible WZ profile without adding CPU-selection UI.

## Context

- Clean local HEAD and inspected GitHub main equal `2142f0f628c3c71814a99d5169153fa94c3d605d`. Relevant paths include `cpu.rs`, `lib.rs`, native CPU/stack/fetch tests, `docs/architecture.md` and compiled-Wasm browser tests.
- Concrete specification-derived reproduction: with carry set and zero at 4000h, execute `LD A,(27FFh); LD HL,4000h; BIT 0,(HL)`. WZ becomes 2800h and survives the immediate HL load. Expected F=7Dh; static inspection predicts current F=55h. This sequence was not executed during planning.
- The [2006 physical-chip investigation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/floooh/emu-info/master/z80/memptr_eng.txt) establishes the BIT dependency and instruction update families. The [expanded upstream table](https://github.com/redcode/Z80/wiki/MEMPTR) supplies the consolidated rules.
- Resolve the historical block-I/O conflict using [z80test correction #3 and its discussion](https://github.com/raxoft/z80test/pull/3): nonterminal INIR/INDR/OTIR/OTDR iterations set WZ to the ED instruction address plus one. The discussion reports Zilog/NEC confirmation; version 1.2a corrected affected expectations. [Pinned redcode implementation](https://github.com/redcode/Z80/blob/e2de436e61d1ca14687795d6392fea926a5a8923/sources/Z80.c) corroborates this. The previously inspected pinned openMSX implementation retains the older rule and is unsuitable as the sole oracle here.
- Open Issues/PRs are empty. Earlier #33 and #43 concern fetch waits and stack ordering. Existing tests are present but lack WZ sequence coverage. PR #72 and its saved validation report 299 Rust/202 browser passes; inspected CI step metadata reports success. Detailed logs were not re-inspected, and no builds/tests were run here.
- Scope is WZ and BIT flags. Q-dependent SCF/CCF behavior, additional block-repeat flag corrections, arbitrary IM0 expansion and access-phase synchronization remain separate gaps. Physical reset-state universality and commercial playability are not claimed.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Independently implement and document a complete WZ update/preservation table for supported instructions: indirect accumulator and absolute word loads/stores, 16-bit arithmetic, EX (SP), RRD/RLD, indexed memory operations, branches/calls/returns/RST, immediate/C-port I/O, block instructions and interrupt entry. Distinguish old/new register values, full-word wrapping and accumulator-store low-byte wrapping. Define deterministic initialization across construction/reset and preserve state through cloning; identify initialization policy separately from measured hardware behavior.
- [ ] Cover taken/untaken conditional paths: JP/CALL load WZ even when untaken; untaken JR/DJNZ/RET and indirect JP preserve it. NMI, IM1/IM2 and returns use their resolved destinations. Supported IM0 follows the supplied instruction's semantics, including WZ preservation for JP (HL).
- [ ] Implement repeat/final distinctions: LDI/LDD preserve WZ; CPI/CPD adjust previous WZ; nonterminal repeating blocks set ED-address+1. Terminal input uses pre-decrement BC±1; terminal output uses post-decrement BC±1. Cover compare-match termination, exhausted counters, ignored prefixes and address wrapping.
- [ ] Add original native sequence vectors with literal independent expectations, including the reproduction above, all eight BIT numbers, both carry states, opposing operand/address/WZ bits, indexed displacement boundaries, preservation sequences and low-byte carry/borrow exposed through later CPI/CPD and BIT. Cover every documented update family. Internal-state assertions may supplement observable probes.
- [ ] Exercise intermediate repeat state and interrupt boundaries. Use opcode-overwrite sequences for repeated input and/or the existing standalone IM0 JP (HL) capability to observe WZ without overwriting it. Add MSX1/MSX2 Machine coverage and an original compiled-Wasm diagnostic exposing captured flags through existing observable output at both hosting roots, including Reset. Require no new debug ABI or proprietary firmware.
- [ ] Coordinator records meaningful baseline failures and corrected passes before merge. Preserve documented flags, unrelated flag behavior, bus access order, refresh/EI/HALT behavior, both fetch policies, returned cycles and `tstates`. Preserve video/audio clocks, disk safety, SRAM persistence, firmware/slot ownership, browser lifecycle and provenance. Update relevant accuracy documentation and attribute sources without copying emulator implementation code.
- [ ] Coordinator completes README checks before merge: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, with documented setup as needed. Review the complete diff and evidence against this Issue, resolve blocking findings, and distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Before merge, compare original vectors with a pinned independent emulator or adapt corrected z80test MEMPTR cases with proper attribution and deterministic I/O. Its Spectrum harness and incomplete MEMPTR coverage require care. These comparisons were not performed here; hardware access and commercial gameplay are unnecessary prerequisites.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
